C-01.summary: Re-dating and single-step supersession are quarantined and released correctly (RN02, RN02b, A01). A two-step supersession chain is admitted and approved in a second period (X01).

C-02.summary: RN01 direct: every decision type, dispositions and finalization refuse under lock; audited reopen required.

C-03.summary: RN03 adapted and A09: identical work reuses the artifact and keeps its rejection; contributors append outside the hash.

C-04.summary: RN04, RN05, RN05b direct and X15: version suppliers, configuration authors and cited-evidence suppliers stay barred. One P2 residual for unlinked rule versions.

C-06.summary: RN07 adapted: all service attempts refused with 403.

RT14b.note: The original script prints OK on current source without reaching its starting state. Accepted on the strengthened adapted probe and independent fault injection.

RN02.reason: The only change is the empty freshness predicate, replaced by the explicit no-evidence form that RV-11 itself provides. Issuer, independent approver, schedule and every verdict expression are unchanged. The probe then runs to completion and its lock, recurrence and reopen conditions hold.

RN03.reason: Same single change. The identity, rejection, contributor and 403 conditions are unchanged and hold.

RN07.reason: Same single change, on a mandate that is deliberately left unapproved. The service approval attempt is refused with 403 by the grant check, not by an invalid mandate. The service-created mandate with {} is untouched and is refused with 403 by the human check, which runs before freshness validation.

RT12a.reason: The newer delivery changes the receipt, so RV-12 requires a hold. The helper first asserts the hold and the disclosed history, then obtains acceptance from the existing dispositioner, who supplied neither version. No grant is added. The original ordering conditions are unchanged.

RT14a.reason: The shared helper adds the candidate receipts only when a distinct-purchases call uses default evidence. The explicit empty-evidence negative is untouched and still refused. All final conditions are unchanged.

RT14b.reason: Evidence now names the candidate receipt, still without the statement. The added assertions make the probe fail when its starting state is not reached. My own fault injection confirms: refusal of D1, refusal of D2 and an ineligible D1 each give ERROR, exit 1, before the third charge is constructed; the valid path gives OK, exit 0.

RG0.reason: Peer receipts are cited for the two distinct-purchases decisions, and the corrected TX-009 receipt is accepted only after its hold and history are asserted. Expected counts, the hand calculation and the isolation conditions are unchanged. My independent M2 reaches the same result by the same route.

dispositions obey activity and account type; valid credit, settlement, transfer, fee and interest paths still work
distinct purchases needs every candidate receipt, binds the exact candidate set, and lapses when a new candidate arrives
excluding a duplicate frees the surviving charge with full lineage; revocation restores both holds and the earlier rejection
a cosmetic re-proposal keeps the earlier rule author in the item lineage; a different historical category does not
freshness must be stated and well formed; explicit no-evidence authority is independently approved and audited
a revised receipt is disclosed and held; suppliers cannot accept it; acceptance lapses on a further change; referral never clears
statement assurance is disclosed; missing line ids need an approved exception; a missing or quarantined prior statement cannot pass
the rule record shows normalised aliases, collisions, status and effective end; own-row evidence is refused
a second package names the one it replaces; one package governs; the first stays byte-identical; acknowledgement cannot clear stale work
a second supersession step does not release a charge that is still quarantined behind a locked origin
an exclusion does not outlive the charge it pointed to, and two charges cannot both be excluded unseen
replacing a receipt under a new key is treated like revising it
a statement re-supplied to agree with the population is disclosed as revised evidence
the supplier of a candidate receipt cited in a distinct-purchases decision cannot review the item it supports
a mandate is not suspended merely because new evidence falls after a rule date that was already approved
when a superseding source is itself removed, the charge it replaced does not vanish unseen
